Oncology / Cancer supportive care · published research

Cancer pain

In a Walker-256 tumor-pain rat experiment, the 1 J laser group had lower edema and favorable IL-10 and inflammatory-marker findings; however, the abstract describes a significant reduction in pain threshold without a clear direction, despite concluding analgesia.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

In a Walker-256 tumor-pain rat experiment, the 1 J laser group had lower edema and favorable IL-10 and inflammatory-marker findings; however, the abstract describes a significant reduction in pain threshold without a clear direction, despite concluding analgesia.

Summary of the Evidence

One unique publication reports a single Walker-256 tumor-pain experiment in rats. It compared control and nimesulide groups with laser groups receiving 1, 3, or 6 J, with six animals per group. These are treatment arms within one experiment, not independent studies. No clinical cancer-pain trial or separate cell experiment was identified.

Human and clinical evidence

No direct human PBM study for cancer pain was identified in the category. The rat experiment therefore cannot establish pain relief in people or compare PBM with clinical analgesics (Petrellis et al. 2020).

Animal evidence

The study used a Walker-256 tumor model. In the 1 J arm, the authors reported reduced edema, higher IL-10, and lower COX-2 and Bdkrb1 expression. They described an analgesic effect comparable to nimesulide, but the abstract also says the pain threshold was significantly reduced without clearly stating whether this means more or less pain sensitivity. That direction is internally unclear and should not be converted into a definite behavioral benefit.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone in-vitro or ex-vivo study was identified. The cytokine and inflammatory-marker measurements are part of the rat experiment, not separate laboratory publications.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The intervention was a 660 nm red laser. The database reports an irradiance of 3.57 W/cm², a 0.028 cm² beam area, and tested energy doses of 1, 3, and 6 J. The favorable biomarker and edema findings centered on the 1 J group. This localized animal exposure does not establish a human dose or clinical analgesic effect.

Interpretation

The findings are preclinical and include a favorable edema and biomarker pattern, alongside an unclear pain-threshold result. Human cancer-pain efficacy remains untested in this evidence set.

Evidence strength in source summaryPain-related outcomes in a Walker-256 rat model: Very low Human pain relief: No direct evidence identified
Publications and records1 unique title

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Evidence consists of one rat experiment with small groups and no human study in this indication. The abstract reports an ambiguous direction for its pain-threshold endpoint even though the authors interpret the intervention as analgesic. Replication with prespecified behavioral outcomes, clear direction, and human safety and efficacy studies would be needed.
